version.changelog:
- Added explicit support for multi-agent orchestration and ultracode, enabling fan-out for parallel legacy codebase cleanup.
- Clarified compatibility section for Claude Code and Codex.
- Introduced a new "paths" field to specify lint-relevant files.
- Updated metadata version to 1.4.0.
- Removed obsolete skill-card.md.

llm.summary: This skill gives Go linting guidance and uses normal linting tools, with a few disclosed operational cautions but no evidence of hidden, deceptive, destructive, or unrelated behavior.

dimensions.detail: Bash access for go, golangci-lint, and git is proportionate for this purpose; automatic --fix runs and legacy cleanup agents can mutate source files, so users should run them in a clean working tree.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill discloses golangci-lint as a dependency and includes package-manager metadata, but also suggests go install with @latest, which is mutable and should be pinned for reproducible installation.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The activation description is somewhat broad and includes general code-quality phrases plus go vet/staticcheck/revive, but the runtime instructions stay focused on golangci-lint configuration, lint output, nolint usage, and Go lint cleanup.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No cross-session persistence, privilege escalation, credential access, memory writes, services, scheduled tasks, or hidden background installation behavior were found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The requested capabilities align with Golang lint setup and cleanup: reading and editing Go/config files, running go, golangci-lint, and git commands, and using agents for larger lint cleanup tasks.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Before installing, prefer a pinned golangci-lint version instead of @latest, review changes before accepting any --fix output, and invoke the skill for Go linting tasks rather than unrelated development work.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: The broad trigger wording is real but tied to Go linting and code-quality setup; it is best treated as a scoping caution rather than evidence of purpose-mismatched behavior.
[T08] expected: The @latest golangci-lint install instruction is a supply-chain reproducibility risk, but installing the linter is expected for this skill and there is no evidence the artifact ships or executes malicious code.
